# The Invisible Institution Behind One Collection — complete editable platform copy

## 1. LONG VIDEO
Follow one look backward from runway image to research, pattern, sample, fitting, sourcing, production, styling, image, press, sales, and archive. Put VERIFIED, INFERENCE, PROPOSAL, and UNRESOLVED on screen; never invent a role because the industry usually has one.

## 2. SHORT 01
“The designer is the headline. The collection is an institution.” Reveal one handoff at a time, ending with the missing fields: pay, approval, credit, ownership, remedy.

## 3. SHORT 02
“A credit list is not a power map.” Split preferred public credit from contract role, decision authority, compensation, and correction rights.

## 4. CAROUSEL
ONE LOOK / WHO RESEARCHED? / WHO PATTERNED? / WHO SAMPLED? / WHO FIT? / WHO MADE? / WHO STYLED? / WHO IMAGED? / WHO APPROVED? / WHO WAS PAID? / WHO OWNS WHAT? / WHO CAN CORRECT?

## 5. NEWSLETTER
Subject: The institution hiding behind one collection. Give readers the constellation worksheet and explain why actual records—not romantic assumptions—must populate it.

## 6. CONTRIBUTOR REVIEW
A private pre-publication sheet for every named person to verify spelling, role, scope, confidentiality, preferred credit, and unresolved dispute without forcing agreement on ownership.

## Claim ledger
- **VERIFIED:** FIT preserves an oral history in which patternmaking faculty discuss specialized training, slopers, industry practice, technology, union history, and intergenerational textile-work experience. (S72)
- **VERIFIED:** A public Mossimo–Target agreement allocates design services, design materials, approvals, channels, publicity, manufacture-related obligations, and trademark uses between named parties. (S77)
- **INFERENCE:** One collection should be credited and governed as a constellation of roles and records rather than as proof that a single visible author performed every kind of work. (S72, S76, S77)

## Publication discipline
Use the copy as written with the package's rendered social artwork. Preserve captions, alt text, creator and institution credits, canonical URLs, evidence labels, labor and jurisdiction limits, participant correction, and counsel or specialist boundaries.
